text:
- chief complaint: the patient wants to quit smoking and has had difficulty doing so.
- history of present illness: the patient started smoking in high school and now smokes about 1.5 packs daily, with the first cigarette within an hour of waking. They quit cold turkey for almost a year, but relapsed during a stressful period at work. They are motivated to quit before the birth of their first child. Their history includes gout and type 2 diabetes.
- physical examination: vitals are within normal limits (BP 128/88, HR 68, RR 16, SpO2 98% on room air). Heart shows regular rate and rhythm with a known 2/6 systolic murmur, to be monitored. Lungs are clear and equal bilaterally without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. No lymphadenopathy or carotid bruit.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: nicotine dependence and difficulty quitting smoking; stress related to work and the upcoming birth of their child.
- new medications prescribed or changed: nicotine patch 21 mg daily starting on the quit date (next Monday), with the dose to be tapered over time; continue allopurinol unchanged.
- follow-up instructions: return in two weeks to reassess the nicotine patch dose; rotate patch application sites daily; get a hemoglobin A1c at the next blood draw; continue diet and exercise for diabetes; monitor stress and watch gout-triggering foods; keep the quit date.
